issues.display_title: Issue #213: feat(stitching): manual field of view (FOV) override with auto default
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

Enable optional manual override of the lens horizontal field of view. By default, FOV is extracted automatically from EXIF metadata. For manual lenses without electronic contacts (e.g., Samyang/Rokinon, TTArtisan), users can manually input the FOV in degrees.

UI Specifications

  • Control: Toggle + Numeric input field in Advanced Settings.
  • Label: \Lens FOV (Field of View)\
  • Options:
    • Auto (From EXIF) — (Default, input disabled/hidden)
    • Manual — Numeric stepper/input with range \100.0° – 240.0°\ (default: \180.0°).

Binary Attributes & CLI Flags

  • CLI Flag: --fov \
  • Default Behavior: Flag omitted when set to \Auto\ (binary computes FOV per image from focal length & sensor size).

Acceptance Criteria

  • When set to \Auto, --fov\ is not passed to the CLI command.
  • When \Manual\ is enabled, valid float values (e.g., --fov 185.5) are validated and forwarded.

issues.display_title: Issue #211: feat(stitching): AI feature matcher (LightGlue) with cpfind fallback
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

Integrate deep learning feature matching (SuperPoint + LightGlue) as the default alignment algorithm. This prevents matching failures on low-texture surfaces (plain white walls, smooth ceilings, narrow hallways) where traditional SIFT (\cpfind) returns 0 control points.

UI Specifications

  • Control: Dropdown / Radio group in Settings panel.
  • Label: \Feature Matcher\
  • Options:
    1. LightGlue (\lightglue) — (Default / Recommended for plain surfaces)
    2. cpfind (\hugin\ / \cpfind)

Binary Attributes & CLI Flags

  • CLI Flag: --matcher <lightglue|hugin>\
  • Default Value: \lightglue\
  • Supporting Flags & Files:
    • \models/lightglue_matcher.py\
    • --lightglue-device <auto|cpu|cuda|mps>\ (default: ^Guto)
    • --lightglue-max-points \ (default: \100)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Backend passes --matcher lightglue\ by default.
  • Python script \lightglue_matcher.py\ is included in the models directory.
  • If Python/LightGlue dependencies are missing, graceful error reporting prompts the user or offers fallback to classic SIFT.

issues.display_title: Issue #212: feat(stitching): high-precision live step telemetry and batch ETA
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-09-04.at.10.45.37.mov

Description

The updated \ isheye-stitch\ binary outputs execution time measurements per pipeline step in stdout. The frontend should leverage this telemetry to display real-time step progress and calculate a significantly more accurate remaining batch ETA.

UI Specifications

  • Queue Card Display:
    • Step status badge: e.g., \Step 7/8: Blending with Multiblend (12s)\
    • Dynamic progress bar reflecting the active step duration rather than a static percentage jump.
  • Queue Board Header: Real-time ETA calculated from completed steps and historical averages.

Binary Attributes & Output Format

  • Stdout Telemetry: [Step n/8] completed in <x.xx>s\
  • Step Milestone Weighting:
    1. \pto_gen\ (~1%)
    2. \cpfind\ / \lightglue\ (~10%)
    3. \cpclean\ (~1%)
    4. ^Gutooptimiser\ (~2%)
    5. \pano_modify\ (~1%)

    6. ona\ (~20%)
    7. \ lender\ (Multiblend / GPU / Enblend) (~45%)
    8. \ ormat conversion\ (~20%)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Backend regex captures step number and elapsed step seconds, streaming it via \stitching-progress\ IPC event.
  • \PanoramaCard\ and \QueueBoard\ update smoothly without jumping backwards.

issues.main_description_html:
Demo

Description:

Implement an anti-tamper authentication mechanism within pano.exe to prevent users from extracting the binary and running it directly as a standalone CLI outside the desktop application.

QA Tester Summary - Issue #230: Implement Time-Based Dynamic Token/Handshake Protection for pano.exe Execution

Status: Passed

Real Account Tested testergothru@gmail.com
Test Coverage White Box, Gray Box, Black Box (Real Installed Desktop App Flow)
Final Verdict Passed

1. Technical Evaluation & Verification

  • Root Cause / Background: To prevent unauthorized standalone extraction and external CLI execution of the proprietary stitching binary pano.exe, a time-based dynamic handshake (HS1) is implemented. Upon launch, pano.exe challenges stdout with a 64-hex nonce and expects HMAC-SHA256(K, nonce || tw_le64) on stdin within 300s windowing tolerance, exiting with code 42 if verification fails.
  • Changes Made & Verified:
    • src-tauri/src/commands/protected_spawn.rs: Implemented spawn_with_handshake managing background reader threads, HS_EXIT_CODE = 42, TW_SECONDS = 300, and HmacSha256 time-window token generation.
    • src-tauri/src/commands/stitching_alin.rs: Integrates spawn_with_handshake into both Phase 1 (pano create) and Phase 2 (pano render), mapping exit code 42 to the dedicated Engine verification failed error.
    • Full End-to-End User Flow Verified: App Launch → Authentication with testergothru@gmail.com → Edit Menu → Stitch 360 Panorama → Select Stitcher Alin engine → Queue panorama with HS1 protected spawning.

issues.display_title: Issue #240: feat(stitching): Add External Multiblend blending engine to Stitcher Alin (pano.exe)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary & Objective

Implement external Multiblend blending support for the Stitcher Alin (pano.exe) stitching pipeline, enabling high-performance multi-band blending via arms-length child process invocation without licensing contamination (ADR-Multiblend Exclusion Amendment 1).

Scope of Work

  1. Engine Rebuild (pano.exe):

    • Rebuilt protected pano.exe from GoThruMedia/pano-stitcher-a@main with HS1 challenge-response protection enabled (--protection secret).
    • Supports CLI flags --blend external, --external-executable <path>, and --keep-external-layers.
    • Bypasses quarter-power internal blend space and exports standard sRGB TIFF layers with associated alpha masks to temp directory.

  2. Backend Rust Integration (gothru-photo-studio-tauri):

    • Extended StitchConfig and parse_config in src-tauri/src/commands/stitching.rs to whitelist 'external' for alin_blend and parse alin_external_executable.
    • Updated stitching_alin.rs to construct --blend external --external-executable <path> render argv.
    • Implemented zero-configuration resolution defaulting to bundled fisheye-stitch/models/multiblend.exe when no manual path is supplied.
    • Fail-fast hard error when no binary is found (no silent degradation to internal multiband).

  3. Frontend & Settings UI:

    • Added External Multiblend option to AlinBlendMethod dropdown in Settings.tsx.
    • Added custom executable path input in Settings with helper text.
    • Updated Redux slice (stitchingSlice.ts), payload assembly (useStitching.ts), IPC type definitions, and localized strings across 18 languages in src/locales/*.json.

  4. Testing & Quality Gate:

    • Rust integration tests: cargo test --test test_stitching_alin_external_blend (7/7 passed).
    • Security handshake test: cargo test --test test_pano_handshake (7/7 passed, including bundled pano.exe).
    • Frontend tests: Redux slice & payload builder unit tests (11/11 passed).
    • Strict typecheck: tsc --noEmit (clean).

Verification & Handshake Status

  • Standalone fail-closed execution verified (exit code 42 without handshake responder).
  • Handshake with Rust responder verified (exit 0).
  • External blend TIFF layer export & multiblend execution verified against real datasets.
